- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5–10% below peak to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–3 day lag correction by reducing forecast slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or low values, model tends to underestimate; apply a 1–2% upward bias to counteract pessimism.
- When sentiment is high and price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; add a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to prevent premature sell-off.
